summary: This codebase follows a layered architecture where the API layer handles HTTP requests and responses, while business logic coordinates application workflows. Data storage and external services are consumed by business logic, with all layers depending on shared utilities and configuration; infrastructure tooling manages deployment and environment setup, and tests validate interactions across layers.

root.label: Architecture
root.description: This codebase follows a layered architecture where the API layer handles HTTP requests and responses, while business logic coordinates application workflows. Data storage and external services are consumed by business logic, with all layers depending on shared utilities and configuration; infrastructure tooling manages deployment and environment setup, and tests validate interactions across layers.

children.label: API
children.description: The API component exposes HTTP endpoints for external clients, organizing features like GitHub, Storybook, User, and Architecture under versioned routers to handle request routing and response formatting.
children.insight: Clean separation: Each feature has its own router and schema, minimizing coupling and enabling independent development.

children.label: features
children.description: The features component organizes API endpoints into domain-specific modules (github, storybook, user, architecture, ai), each with its own router, schema, and init files to enable clean separation of concerns.

children.label: github
children.description: The github component provides API endpoints and data validation schemas for interacting with GitHub's API, handling authentication, repository data, and webhooks within the application. It acts as a clean interface between the core system and external GitHub services.

children.label: storybook
children.description: The storybook component provides a local development environment for UI components by exposing them via a router endpoint, allowing designers and developers to visualize and test components in isolation. It relies on schema definitions to validate component data and uses __init__.py to expose public APIs.
children.insight: router.py is the entry point and de facto god file, as it imports and registers all storybook routes and schema validations

children.label: user
children.description: The user component defines the data schema and routing logic for user-related operations, serving as a self-contained module for handling user data structures and HTTP endpoints.

children.label: architecture
children.description: This component defines the routing and data schema for architectural features, serving as the foundational layer that structures how requests are routed and validated. It enables consistent, type-safe interaction between the router and underlying data models.

children.label: api
children.description: The api component exposes HTTP endpoints via a versioned router (v1_router.py) that delegates requests to the features layer, acting as the sole interface between external clients and internal business logic.

children.label: common
children.description: The common component provides shared routing logic and centralized error handling for the API layer, ensuring consistent request processing and error responses across all endpoints.

children.label: Business Logic
children.description: The Business Logic component orchestrates GitHub-specific analysis workflows, including dependency parsing, call graph extraction, and architecture synthesis, serving as the core engine that transforms raw code data into structured insights for downstream consumers.
children.insight: tight coupling between service modules in src/features/github/services, where architecture_service, flow_service, and dependency_service explicitly depend on each other's internal logic rather than abstractions.

children.label: features
children.description: The features component encapsulates business logic for analyzing GitHub repositories, including dependency scanning, call graph extraction, and architectural insights, serving as a modular hub for specialized service modules.
children.insight: Clean separation: Each service file (e.g., dependency_parser.py, call_graph_extractor.py) handles a distinct analytical concern with no cross-dependencies.

children.label: github
children.description: The github component analyzes code repositories by extracting symbols, dependencies, and call graphs to generate architectural overviews and flow insights. It serves as the core engine for understanding code structure within the features layer.
children.insight: service.py is the clear entry point and orchestrator, tightly coupling all service modules into a unified workflow

children.label: Data & Storage
children.description: The Data & Storage component manages all database schema definitions, migrations, and ORM models for entities like users, repositories, storybooks, and architecture results, serving as the authoritative source of truth for persistent data.
children.insight: Clean separation: Models and repositories are cleanly divided by feature (e.g., github/, storybook/, architecture/), with migrations versioned and isolated, enabling safe, incremental schema evolution.

children.label: src
children.description: This component manages data models and repository logic for core features like User, GitHub, Architecture, and Storybook, serving as the central persistence layer for the application.

children.label: features
children.description: The features componentorganizes domain-specific logic for user, github, storybook, and architecture modules, each with paired models and repositories to encapsulate data structures and data access patterns. It acts as the business logic layer between the database and higher-level services.

children.label: db
children.description: The db component manages database session configuration, base model definitions, and reusable model mixins, serving as the foundational data access layer for the application.
children.insight: tight coupling between base.py and base_class.py, which together define the core ORM structure used by all models

children.label: migrations
children.description: This component manages database schema changes through Alembic migrations, ensuring the data model evolves consistently with code changes in the src module. It defines and applies database versions to track structural changes like new tables and columns.

children.label: External Services
children.description: This component manages interactions with external AI services, specifically AWS Bedrock, and orchestrates story-based learning workflows through a dedicated agent system, acting as the bridge between business logic and external AI providers.
children.insight: src/features/ai/bedrock.py is the single entry point for all external AI calls, creating a clear abstraction but risking tight coupling if not carefully versioned.

children.label: Infrastructure & Tooling
children.description: This component manages the foundational infrastructure and tooling required to deploy and operate the application, including network security groups, load balancers, S3 buckets, RDS, and Lambda functions via Terraform, alongside Docker and Python tooling for local and staging environments.

children.label: terraform
children.description: This component manages AWS infrastructure as code using Terraform, providing reusable modules for core services like security groups, S3, RDS, Lambda, IAM, and ACM to enable consistent and scalable cloud deployments.

children.label: modules
children.description: The modules component contains reusable, self-contained Terraform modules that encapsulate infrastructure patterns for AWS resources like security groups, RDS, S3, Lambda, IAM, and others, enabling consistent and portable infrastructure provisioning.

children.label: appsync
children.description: The appsync component defines and provisions an AWS AppSync API using a GraphQL schema, auto-generated resolvers from OpenAPI specifications, and VTL templates to handle data source interactions. It serves as a reusable module for exposing backend services through a unified GraphQL interface.
children.insight: generate-from-openapi.js and generate-vtl.js form the entry point for resolver logic generation, tightly coupling API specification changes to resolver code generation.

children.label: ses
children.description: This component manages Amazon SES (Simple Email Service) configuration, including email sending permissions via IAM roles and a custom HTML template for user invites.
children.insight: Clean separation between SES core configuration and IAM permissions, with the template file cleanly isolated for reuse.

children.label: lambda
children.description: The lambda module defines an AWS Lambda function powered by Python code (s3_to_celery.py) that processes S3 events and triggers Celery tasks, encapsulating all infrastructure and code in a reusable Terraform module.

children.label: security_groups
children.description: This component defines and manages AWS security groups to control inbound and outbound network traffic for resources within the VPC. It serves as a reusable, parameterized module for consistent security policy application across environments.

children.label: alb
children.description: The alb component defines an Application Load Balancer in AWS, handling HTTP/HTTPS traffic routing to target groups with configurable security groups, subnets, and listener rules.

children.label: rds
children.description: The rds component defines and provisions an Amazon RDS database instance using Terraform, encapsulating configuration inputs and output values for reuse across environments. It serves as a modular, reusable module for database infrastructure without direct dependencies or consumers at this level.

children.label: s3
children.description: This component manages AWS S3 bucket creation and configuration, encapsulating infrastructure as code for consistent bucket setup across environments. It serves as a reusable module for defining bucket properties like versioning, encryption, and access policies.

children.label: iam
children.description: The iam component manages AWS Identity and Access Management resources, defining roles, policies, and permissions in a reusable module format. It serves as a foundation for securing access across other AWS services by centralizing IAM configuration.

children.label: acm
children.description: The ACM component manages AWS Certificate Manager certificates, provisioning and validating SSL/TLS certificates for use in other AWS services.

children.label: dynamodb
children.description: The dynamodb component defines a reusable Terraform module for provisioning Amazon DynamoDB tables with configurable parameters like throughput, attributes, and global secondary indexes. It encapsulates the infrastructure logic to ensure consistent table creation across environments.

children.label: elasticache
children.description: The elasticache component manages AWS ElastiCache Redis clusters, abstracting configuration details like node type, size, and subnet groups into reusable Terraform modules. It serves as a standardized entry point for provisioning in-memory caching infrastructure across environments.

children.label: other
children.description: This component contains a set of reusable Terraform modules for AWS services including EBS volumes, SSM, Secrets Manager, Route53, VPC, EC2, SQS, Cognito, and SNS, providing modular, parameterized infrastructure definitions. It serves as a library of standardized infrastructure building blocks with clear input/output contracts.

children.label: envs
children.description: The envs component manages distinct Terraform configurations for development, staging, and production environments, each with isolated backend, variables, and script files to ensure environment-specific infrastructure deployment. It enables consistent, repeatable provisioning while maintaining separation of concerns across environments.

children.label: dev
children.description: The dev component sets up and manages the development environment using Terraform, including infrastructure provisioning and environment cleanup scripts. It serves as the isolated, reproducible baseline for development work.
children.insight: Entry point is main.tf with backend.tf defining state storage, ensuring consistent state management for dev infrastructure.

children.label: prod
children.description: The prod component configures the production environment using Terraform, defining infrastructure variables, backend settings, and main resources. It serves as the authoritative deployment target for production workloads.
children.insight: backend.tf is the entry point, enforcing remote state management for consistency and collaboration.

children.label: staging
children.description: The staging component defines the infrastructure configuration for the staging environment using Terraform, including variables, backend settings, and main resource definitions. It serves as a dedicated, isolated environment for testing before production deployment.

children.label: scripts
children.description: This component provides templated startup scripts for EC2 instances across different environments (dev, staging, production), enabling environment-specific configuration during instance bootstrapping.

children.label: notebooks
children.description: The notebooks component contains Jupyter notebooks and associated output files used for exploring, prototyping, and documenting the Story Book Agent's architecture and behavior. It serves as a sandbox for iterative development and analysis but has no runtime dependencies or consumers in the current system.
children.insight: Entry point: notebooks/story_book_agent.ipynb with supporting outputs in notebooks/outputs/storybook/

children.label: nginx
children.description: Nginx serves as a reverse proxy and web server, handling incoming HTTP requests and routing them based on configurations defined in conf.d/default.conf and managed via nginx.conf. It is a foundational component for traffic management in the infrastructure.

children.label: scripts
children.description: The scripts component provides utility tools for environment management, repository context dumping, and toolchain validation, serving as isolated helper scripts for developer and CI workflows.

children.label: docker
children.description: This component packages the application into a Docker container using a customized base image and bootstraps it with an entrypoint script that handles runtime initialization and configuration.

children.label: Shared & Config
children.description: This component provides shared configuration, utilities, and middleware that standardize logging, authentication, error handling, and environment-specific settings across the entire system, acting as the foundational layer for consistency and reliability.
children.insight: tight coupling between auth/jwt.py, auth/cognito.py, and utils/auth_middleware.py creates dependency friction when swapping auth providers.

children.label: config
children.description: The config component manages environment-specific settings and constants for the application, providing a structured way to load and override configurations based on deployment environments like dev, staging, and prod.

children.label: utils
children.description: The utils component provides shared low-level utilities for authentication, logging, and JWT verification, acting as a foundational support layer for the application stack.

children.label: middleware
children.description: The middleware component handles cross-cutting concerns such as user context propagation, CORS, rate limiting, and request logging, acting as an intercepting layer between incoming HTTP requests and application logic. It relies on config and auth to enforce security and behavioral policies consistently across the service.

children.label: auth
children.description: The auth component handles authentication and authorization logic using AWS Cognito and JWT tokens, providing utilities for permission validation and JWT generation/validation. It acts as the centralized authority for user identity and access control within the application.

children.label: common
children.description: The common component provides shared exception definitions and initialization logic for the application, serving as a foundational layer for consistent error handling across modules.

children.label: Tests
children.description: The Tests component provides the testing infrastructure for the application, including fixtures and configuration to support integration and unit tests across Shared & Config, Data & Storage, and API modules. It acts as the entry point for running and managing all test suites.
